rows.estimation_basis: Estimates are directly derived from the historical reference project 'Fleet Tracking Portal for a Logistics Operator' (id=001-logistics-fleet-portal, 3,400 hours). Core functional modules were mapped directly: Auth/RBAC (160h baseline adjusted to 140-180h for 3 municipalities), Live Map (420h baseline adapted to 380-460h), Alerts Engine (380h baseline adapted to 360-440h to accommodate stop geofencing alongside idle alerts), and Fleet CRUD (240h baseline retained at 200-260h). The telematics ingestion module was adjusted downward from 520h to 240-300h because the client utilizes a single GPS tracker vendor rather than three separate vendors, eliminating multi-vendor normalization overhead while preserving queue resilience. Reporting (360h baseline adapted to 320-400h) and DevOps (220h baseline adapted to 180-240h) reflect standard production requirements. QA, UAT, and stabilization (700h baseline adjusted to 520-660h) were maintained as a primary effort allocation to validate geospatial edge cases and municipal sign-off.

No historical reference projects were provided in the RFP. Estimates are derived bottom-up based on standard engineering lifecycle parameters for mid-scale IoT ingestion and GIS solutions. Effort accounts for architecture, backend/frontend engineering, geospatial QA simulation, and multi-tenant stabilization. Given the lack of prior vendor integration benchmarks, an estimated variance buffer of approximately 25-30% is reflected across feature ranges.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 002-fintech-kyc-onboarding (KYC Onboarding Platform for a Digital Bank, 5,200 total hours over 26 weeks). The requirements align closely across document ingestion, verification vendor orchestration, watchlist screening, and back-office case management. The reference allocations were mapped module-by-module (e.g., Onboarding Wizard at 440-520h vs. 480h reference; Back-Office Review Console at 680-760h vs. 720h reference; QA/UAT at 1,100-1,280h vs. 1,200h reference). The scope accounts for rigorous financial institution standards, including end-to-end auditability and third-party penetration testing fixes.

No historical reference projects were provided. Estimates were constructed using a bottom-up delivery model derived from industry-standard enterprise financial technology architectures. Effort encompasses the full software delivery lifecycle, including technical discovery, cloud infrastructure provisioning, API integration with third-party KYC/AML vendors, automated and manual QA, security validation, and operational stabilization. A standard uncertainty margin of 25-30% is incorporated across the upper estimates to account for third-party provider integration quirks and compliance review feedback.

Estimates are grounded directly in historical delivery data from 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (id=003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace, 6,100 total hours). The catalogue import pipeline (estimated at 560-680h vs. 620h reference) accounts for irregular dealer spreadsheet feeds and custom field mapping as identified in the reference project's lessons learned. Search and faceted filtering (480-580h vs. 540h reference) mirrors the Elasticsearch aggregation scope for complex attributes. The deposit and Stripe Connect split payment implementation (640-760h vs. 700h reference) aligns with marketplace split-payment workflows. Dealer portal (680-820h vs. 820h reference) and Admin moderation (460-560h vs. 520h reference) are directly adapted. Enterprise punch-out integration (480h in reference) was removed as it is outside agricultural marketplace requirements, while quote workflows were adjusted to inquiry/offer negotiation (440-540h vs. 780h reference). QA/UAT (780-960h vs. 920h reference) and DevOps (340-420h vs. 380h reference) are retained proportionally to ensure production stability.

No specific reference projects were provided for this proposal. The estimate is built bottom-up from general engineering experience delivering multi-tenant marketplace platforms, custom background file processing pipelines, and Stripe Connect split payment architectures. Effort allocations account for total end-to-end human delivery, including technical architecture, UX design, full-stack implementation, automated testing, DevOps provisioning, and user acceptance support. Uncertainty in third-party dealer spreadsheet structures and regulatory payment flows has been factored into the variance between minimum and maximum hours.

Estimates are grounded directly in historical delivery data from Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (Patient Appointment and Telehealth App: 3,900 total hours, 22 weeks duration, utilizing Flutter, FastAPI, PostgreSQL, Twilio Video, and GCP). Core modules such as scheduling (520h reference vs 480-560h current), video consultation (380h reference vs 360-420h current), therapist dashboard (560h reference vs 500-600h current), messaging/notifications (420h reference vs 380-450h current), and QA/store submissions (340h reference vs 340-410h current) have been directly mapped. The reference EHR integration module (480h) was reallocated to engineer the custom Physiotherapy Exercise Regimen Builder and Compliance Tracking Module (400-480h), which is specific to physiotherapy treatment continuity. Infrastructure, DevOps, and HIPAA data isolation remain aligned with historical healthcare baselines.

No reference projects were provided for this proposal; therefore, estimates are derived bottom-up based on industry-standard engineering benchmarks for HIPAA-compliant telehealth applications. Work breakdowns incorporate complete end-to-end delivery lifecycle effort, including systems engineering, backend/frontend development, automated and exploratory QA, cloud security hardening, and app store publishing operations.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project #005 (Internal HR Knowledge Assistant - 1,500 total hours, 10 weeks). While both projects share identical architectural patterns (FastAPI, Qdrant payload-filtered RAG, Angular streaming UI, Azure Entra ID SSO, and evaluation suites), the engineering knowledge base has ~1,500 technical documents (compared to 400 HR documents) featuring complex engineering tables and technical standards nomenclature. We scaled the Document Ingestion module by ~15% (260-310h vs. 240h in reference) and adjusted Access Control (190-230h vs. 180h) to account for project team membership mappings. Other core modules (Retrieval, Chat UI, Evals, DevOps, QA) are matched closely to historical delivery records.

No reference projects were provided. Estimates were developed bottom-up based on industry-standard engineering effort for enterprise RAG platforms, accounting for discovery, backend and frontend development, data ingestion pipelines, Entra ID integration, automated and manual QA, retrieval evaluation benchmarks, DevOps, and stabilization.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against Reference Project 006-saas-analytics-dashboard (Embedded Analytics Dashboard for a SaaS Product, 4,600 total hours across 24 weeks). The scope matches the reference nearly 1:1, including real-time Kafka event streaming (ref: 520h, estimated: 480-560h), ClickHouse data modeling and materialized views (ref: 640h, estimated: 580-680h), tenant-isolated Query API (ref: 560h, estimated: 500-600h), drag-and-drop Angular dashboard builder (ref: 1,000h, estimated: 920-1,100h), scheduled PDF exports (ref: 380h, estimated: 350-420h), DevOps/Terraform (ref: 440h, estimated: 400-480h), load testing (ref: 300h, estimated: 280-340h), and QA/rollout (ref: 760h, estimated: 700-820h). Lessons learned from reference 006 regarding dashboard builder scope inflation and query timeout guardrails have been explicitly incorporated into the risks and architectural design.

Estimates are directly benchmarked against reference project #008-mobile-field-service (Offline-First Field Service App for Technicians, 3600h total). The mobile inspection core, offline data sync layer (760h baseline), photo/signature handling (300h baseline), and QA/pilot activities (400h baseline) match the reference scope and incorporate the recommended 25% buffer for offline edge-case testing. We adjusted down the back-office dispatch/ERP module from the reference (1160h total) to account for the client's simpler customer portal requirements (Asset History + Invoice Download, estimated at 620h-760h combined) while retaining dedicated hours for cloud DevOps, enterprise RBAC, and multi-tenant billing retrieval.

No historical reference projects were provided for this proposal. Significant engineering effort has been allocated specifically to offline data synchronization, network edge-case recovery, and multi-platform QA to account for high architectural complexity in zero-connectivity environments.

Estimates are directly derived from reference benchmarks in corporate training and identity verification. Specifically, core LMS capabilities (user management/SSO at 200-240h, video progress tracking at 280-340h, assessments at 320-380h, certificates at 180-220h, and manager reports at 260-320h) mirror the calibrated modules from Reference Project 007-edtech-lms (2,800 total hours), with SCORM-specific development removed since standard video/quiz compliance was specified. The external identity verification and proof-retention components (IDV vendor integration at 420-500h, PII encryption and audit logging at 380-460h) were calibrated against Reference Project 002-fintech-kyc-onboarding (which recorded 460h for IDV vendor integration and 420h for PII/encryption). DevOps, infrastructure hardening, and rigorous QA/UAT (totaling 800-980h) reflect the high assurance required for regulated compliance training as evidenced in both benchmarks.

Estimates are directly grounded in historical data from Reference Project 'Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (RAG)' (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 total hours, 10 weeks). Core modules such as document ingestion (240-280h), retrieval with reranking (220-260h), and chat UI (260-300h) closely mirror the reference baseline but include slight upward adjustments (+20-40h each) to account for clinical complexity, strict medical citation granularity (section-level), and responsive mobile browser testing across handheld devices. Access control and SSO integration (180-220h and 140-170h) reflect the baseline with additional hardening for hospital department isolation. The evaluation suite (170-210h) incorporates lessons learned regarding outdated document risk by embedding versioning validation into the test suite.

Estimates are grounded in two reference deliveries: Fleet Tracking Portal (001-logistics-fleet-portal) and B2B Marketplace (003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace). Telematics integration (480-620h), live map tracking (400-520h), and geofence alerting (320-420h) are scaled directly from 001's telematics (520h), live map (420h), and alert engine (380h), incorporating lessons on vendor variance and server-side clustering. The load posting, bidding, and carrier onboarding flows adapt modules from 003's quote workflow (780h) and supplier portal (820h), trimmed to focus on freight loads rather than multi-item product catalogs. Stripe split payments (520-680h) draw from 003's Stripe Connect delivery (700h). QA, DevOps, and multi-tenant setup were baselined from historical delivery proportions of both projects.

Estimates are grounded in two historical delivery projects: 'Embedded Analytics Dashboard for a SaaS Product' (006-saas-analytics-dashboard) and 'B2B Marketplace for Industrial Parts' (003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace). The scheduled report and Excel export module (320-420 h) directly adapts the 380 h benchmark from 006, while the query and dashboard development draws on 006's multi-tenant query API (560 h) and dashboard implementation, scaled down appropriately as fixed broker layouts replace a fully custom drag-and-drop widget builder. The file ingestion engine and mapping UI (860-1,090 h combined) are directly informed by 003's catalogue import pipeline (620 h) and its critical lesson learned: heterogeneous supplier feeds require dedicated validation and mapping tools to avoid project creep. Quality assurance, penetration testing, and DevOps reflect the proven effort distributions from both references (combined 700-1,100 h) to guarantee watertight multi-tenant data isolation.

Because no historical reference projects were provided, this estimate is derived bottom-up based on industry-standard engineering benchmarks for secure multi-tenant financial applications. Estimates are strictly calibrated using historical benchmarks from Reference Project 004-healthcare-patient-app (total 3,900 h, 22 weeks). The Flutter cross-platform mobile scope is benchmarked against Project 004's Flutter app (900 h baseline), adjusted to 700-850 h to account for lighter medical UI but adding QR display and local wallet caching. The POS integration is directly derived from Project 004's EHR/HL7 FHIR integration (480 h baseline), mapped to an anti-corruption POS adapter at 420-520 h. Notifications and personal offers are derived from Project 004's notification engine (420 h baseline), estimated at 320-400 h. The Marketing Admin Portal is adapted from Project 004's Doctor Dashboard (560 h baseline) adjusted to 440-540 h for marketing campaign workflows. Security, ledger auditing, and DevOps reuse Project 004's audit and infrastructure standards (300 h baseline scaled down to 220-280 h). QA and store release (340 h in Project 004) are estimated at 300-380 h including till hardware integration tests.

Estimates were calibrated against two historical reference deliveries: 003-ecommerce-b2b-marketplace and 004-healthcare-patient-app. From 003 (which invested 700h in checkout/Stripe and 820h in inventory/supplier portals), we adapted the payment checkout, deposit processing, and inventory catalog down to ~480h-620h total, reflecting a single-shop operational model rather than multi-vendor marketplace split payouts. From 004 (which allocated 520h for scheduling/calendar conflict detection and 560h for practitioner dashboards), we derived our scheduling engine, operational dispatch calendar, and pickup/return module (~520h-680h combined), tailored specifically for physical asset tracking rather than doctor appointments. Dedicated allocations for DevOps (160h-220h) and QA/UAT (240h-320h) reflect real delivery overhead observed across both reference projects.

Estimates were baselined against historical project data from the Internal HR Knowledge Assistant (id=005-hr-internal-ai-assistant, 1,500 total hours). Ingestion and extraction were expanded from the HR assistant baseline (240h) to 260-340h due to the physical scan degradation, image preprocessing, and multi-field OCR required instead of native digital PDF/DOCX parsing. Search retrieval was adapted from the reference's metadata filtering and reranking (200h) to 200-260h to incorporate PostGIS spatial address matching and fuzzy full-text search. UI development was expanded into two distinct applications: the Clerk Back-Office (180-240h) and the Citizen Search Portal (160-220h), exceeding the single Angular chat UI (260h) from the reference. The Certified Copy workflow (payment processing, cryptographic document stamping, and verification) has no direct analogue in the reference and was estimated bottom-up at 220-300h. Security and access control (160-220h), QA/evaluation benchmarking (220-280h), and DevOps/deployment (140-180h) were directly informed by the reference's 180h, 240h, and 140h allotments, scaled to accommodate public municipal compliance.

Estimates are directly informed by two historical benchmarks: 'Fleet Tracking Portal' (id=001-logistics-fleet-portal, 3,400h) and 'Learning Management System' (id=007-edtech-lms, 2,800h). From Reference 007-edtech-lms, the quiz creation and attempt assessment scope (340h + 480h LMS authoring) informs our Quiz Studio (320-400h) and Post-Event Analytics (160-220h). From Reference 001-logistics-fleet-portal, real-time WebSocket fan-out and burst ingestion architecture (420h live map + 700h QA/stabilisation) informs our Real-Time Game Engine (380-460h), High-Throughput Scoring (280-360h), and rigorous QA/Load Testing allocations (440-540h). Adjustments have been made to account for the unique high-concurrency 5,000-player simultaneous ingress requirements of live venue gaming.
